x: The 3000 metres event saw Len Eyre come home in first place followed by Paget and Gordon Pirie and Ray Tooby ran well to finish 5th and was clocked to do 8 min. 33 secs., which was very fast running.
Ian Badiali won the 880 yards in fine style, beating Allen of Ealing H., the Middlesex champion, with Jack Brown and Ray Tooby also behind him.

The Kent championships saw Ray Tooby win the Senior 1 mile with Jack Brown in second place and the time was 4 min. 19.6 secs. "Ginger" Holtum was 2nd in the Middlesex Senior 100 yards championship, and Bob Taylor ran well to finish 2nd in the 880 yards.
Ray Tooby and Bob Taylor also qualified for the 880 yards final and Bob ran a fine race to finish in 2nd place, but Ray was almost run-out and could only struggle in for 6th position.

Their final placing of 13th was not so good as we had expected, although the fact that they were without the help of Ray Tooby, our Junior champion, must have had a disheartening effect on the rest of the team.

Ray Tooby was our next runner and he ran a "blinder" to equal Charlie Smart's record-breaking run on this same stage the previous year. We were now only 37 seconds behind the leaders after being nearly 2 minutes down at the end of the first stage.

The 4 x 1 mile was the main event of the evening and Walton had given out that they were after a new British record. Ray Tooby was our first runner and he gave us the lead from Doug. Wilson, of the Poly, with the Walton runner well back.
The 1 mile also saw only one Belgrave representative in Ray Tooby, but here again he was more than a match for the opposition, and Ray won in the good time of 4 min. 21 secs.

Ray Tooby ran an impressive race to win the 1 mile and his time of 4 min. 18.4 secs. was said to be a new ground record. Ray Tooby set the pace for the first lap but coming down the back straight with 300 yards to go, Davidson and Walker both passed Tooby and these two fought it out until the final 100 yards when Walker went away to win with Davidson and Tooby 2nd and 3rd respectively.
We missed Ray Tooby - who failed to make an appearance - in the 880 yards, but George Davidson carried our colours and came 5th. Jon Burr did not run with his usual zest and did not gain a point.

Brian Hallowell won the mile in 4m. 21.5s. with John Davies 2nd and Ray Tooby 3rd. John took the lead with 220 yards to go but Brian fought back in the home straight and passed John a few yards from the finish.

However, after much persuasion Bill Bird made our three in the 3000 metres team race, but not being at his best he finished well down. Ray Tooby ran well to be placed third (How about that Club Vest Ray?) and George Davidson was fifth.

Ray Tooby,another of our experienced runners who had missed a few Brightons,took over on the flat 5mls.run to Lowfield Heath with three runners in sight.He ran steadily,but his effort lacked spirit,and we made no further headway.We were now 2½ mins down.
Walker, who incidentally, was ill just before the race, in 10th. place, Ray Tooby 11th. and Charlie Dabbs 17th.
Ray Tooby, continuing his welcome return to form, ran very well to finish 12th, only three seconds behind Haslam (T.V.H.). Len Bishop who arrived only just in time for the start, finished 46th.

Jack Brown ran very impressively to win by a full minute from Charlie Walker with Ray Tooby half a minute further back in third place. Steve Charlton, showing much improved form, deservedly won the handicap.
Coming up to four miles Brown had a lead of one hundred yards on Walker, with Dave Baulch a similar distance adrift, followed by Eric Gebbett and Ray Tooby a little way behind.

There our men showed that at least they could hold on to their positions, and after 3 miles Jack had moved up to the twenties, Eric was running extremely well, just outside the hundred; Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Chas Walker and Len Bishop were our scoring team in that order.

Eric handed over to Ray Tooby, who moved up well to place us 3rd, despite clashing with Redrup of Wycombe Phoenix who broke the lap record. Our next man, however, Jack Brown, was to have none of this, and proceeded to smash Redrup's record and put us in the lead with a scintillating run.
Ray Tooby moved up to 4th place on the next stage, and Chas Walker, with an almost identical time, ensured that our next man, Jack Brown, was within striking distance of the leaders.
In Chas Walker, Dave Baulch, Ray Tooby, Pat Newell and Brian Hallowell, to name but a few, we have runners of the class of which champions are made.
Sheffield were again in the lead with T.V.H. second and S.L.H. third. 6th Ray Tooby Ray took over 86 sec. behind the leaders and ran steadily throughout.
